q: In a recursive function on a tree, what is the base case?
options: An empty spot (`null`) returns at once
why: Without `if (!node) return ...` the code reads a property of null and crashes. Write the base case first.

q: What is the difference between preorder, inorder and postorder?
options: Whether you use a stack or a queue
When the node is visited: before its children, between them, or after them
Whether you start at the left or the right leaf
How many children each node has
why: All three are depth first. Only the moment of the visit changes.

q: What does an inorder walk of a binary search tree give?
options: The values in the order they were inserted
why: Left side is smaller, then the node, then the right side is bigger, so the walk comes out sorted.

q: Which data structure does BFS (level order) use, and which does DFS use?
options: BFS a stack, DFS a queue
BFS a queue, DFS a stack (often the call stack)
why: A queue gives back the oldest first, so it finishes a level before the next. A stack goes deep first.

q: Why is checking only that each node fits its parent NOT enough to validate a BST?
options: A value deep on one side can break the rule for a far ancestor
Parents are never compared with children
why: In my test tree 3 sat on the right of 5 and the parent-only check said valid. Pass down a lower and an upper limit.

q: You insert 1, 2, 3, ... 1000 in this order into a plain BST. How tall is the tree?
why: Each new value is bigger than all before, so it always goes right. Search becomes O(n). The same numbers in a shuffled order gave a height of 25.
